The Inquisition ordered an artist to rename a painting of this scene due to its inclusion of foreign soldiers. That painting originally about this scene was altered into a scene focusing on the (*) tax collector Levi by Paolo Veronese. Contrary to most versions, a painting of this scene whose only light sources are a ceiling lamp and a halo was aligned diagonally. Ludovico Sforza commissioned a painting of this scene for the refectory of the Santa Maria delle Grazie, which depicts a salt cellar being tipped over by Judas. For 10 points, name this scene showing Jesus and his Twelve Apostles on the same side of a long table in a mural by Leonardo da Vinci.
2.r: The Last Supper [or L’Ultima Cena; accept Il Cenacolo; prompt on Feast at the House of Levi with "What was the work originally named as?" until Levi is mentioned]

2.q: This painting was inspired by one on the same theme by Peter Paul Rubens that shows three stars above the title figure, who carries a scythe in his right hand. Before Baron Emile d'Erlanger ("ay-MEEL dair-lawn-ZHAY") had this painting transferred from plaster to canvas, it was in a room with paintings of Judith and Holofernes, a witches' sabbath, and the artist's mistress, surnamed Weiss ("vice"). This painting was the direct inspiration for the Pale Man in the film (*) Pan's Labyrinth. It was originally found opposite La Leocadia ("lay-oh-KAH-dee-ah") in the artist's house, the Quinta del Sordo ("KEEN-tah del SOR-doh"). This painting shows a wide-eyed giant against a black background holding up a bloodied, headless corpse. For 10 points, what grotesque painting by Francisco Goya shows the title Roman god eating one of his children?
2.r: Saturn Devouring His Son [or Saturn Devouring His Children or Saturno devorando a su hijo]

2.q: A rumpled carpet appears at the bottom of a Madonna by this painter whose patron is shown with his deceased first wife, his current wife, his daughter, and his two deceased sons. Early in life, this artist and his brother Ambrosius worked as apprentices in Basel ("BAH-zull"). Jesus appears to be giving the viewer the middle finger in an extremely wide painting by this artist that depicts the emaciated (*) body of Christ in the tomb. Scientific instruments, such as a quadrant and a shepherd's dial, and a lute with a broken string are part of the elaborate still life at the center of this artist's painting of Georges de Selve and Jean de Dinteville ("dan-tuh-VEEL"), which includes an anamorphic skull at the bottom. For 10 points, name this painter of The Ambassadors.

According to its artist's studies, this painting was slated to include a sailor drinking wine and a medical student holding a skull. A figure in this artwork was painted to resemble a sculpture of an Oviri goddess that Paul Gauguin gifted to its artist. This "exorcism painting" was created as a compositional rebuttal to Henri Matisse's The Joy of Life. The foreground of this painting, which was first publicly exhibited during the 1916 Salon d'Antin ("dahn-TAHN"), features a triangular table displaying a pile of (*) gray-shaded fruits. Blue curtains drape around this painting's two rightmost figures, whose geometrized faces resemble African masks. Barcelona's red-light district is the setting of, for 10 points, what painting by Pablo Picasso portraying five nude prostitutes?
2.r: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon (“lay DAY-mwah-zell DAH-vee-n’yawn”) [or The Young Ladies of Avignon; accept The Brothel of Avignon or Le Bordel d'Avignon]

2.q: An installation that prominently featured this color was responded to by Arman's installation Full-Up. To create a painting of this color, an artist worked on three stretched canvas collages that were joined and layered with encaustic mixed with beeswax. Paintings of this color were hung on the ceiling of a college dining hall for the first Happening, John Cage's Theater Piece No. 1. It's not blue, but the Iris Clert Gallery was emptied to display an artwork consisting of only this color by (*) Yves Klein titled The Void. Cy Twombly and Robert Rauschenberg collaborated on a series of paintings titled for this color. A flag of this color with 13 stripes but only 48 stars was painted by Jasper Johns. For 10 points, many minimalist artists created works dominated by what color of blank canvases?

A 30 foot sculpture of one of these animals by John Kindness is found at Donegall Quay in Belfast. Salvador Dali's Dream Caused by the Flight of a Bee depicts a tiger being eaten by one of these animals. These animals often appear in the still lives of Willem Ormea. A Pieter Bruegel the Elder engraving shows several small examples of these animals emerging from the mouth of a large one while a man cuts into the large one with a huge knife. A mobile by Alexander Calder pairs the (*) tail of one of these animals with a lobster trap. The left side of a Masaccio fresco in the Brancacci Chapel shows a man in blue retrieving a coin from the mouth of one of these animals. The painting The Tribute Money contains-for 10 points-what aquatic animals often depicted in East Asian art in koi ponds?
2.c: 2018 Florida Spring Tournament (FST) Pkt G. Packet 7 Q19

2.q: This artist is thought to have depicted the daughter of Palma Il Vecchio in Violante. A Satyr who challenged Apollo to a music contest is depicted hanging upside down in this artist's The Flaying of Marsyas. This artist painted the title figure turn into a stag and be mauled by dogs in The Death of (*) Actaeon. This artist of the Danae series depicted an ex-lover of Theseus being rescued by one god followed by a group of drunken revelers in Bacchus and Ariadne. For 10 points, name this Venetian artist of Sacred and Profane Love and Venus of Urbino.

Yann Weymouth designed a museum named for this man that includes works from the collection of Reynolds and Eleanor Morse. In a photo named for and containing this man, three cats and a bucket of water appear suspended in mid-air. That photo of this man by Philippe Halsman includes his painting Leda Atomica. A museum dedicated to this man is in (*) St. Petersburg, Florida and is home to his work The Hallucinogenic Toreador. Another painting by this man includes swarming ants and melting clocks. For 10 points, name this Spanish artist of the surrealist painting The Persistence of Memory.
2.r: Salvador <u>Dali</u> [or Salvador Domingo Felipe Jacinto <u>Dali</u> i Domenech]

2.q: A purple one of these objects appears on the ground between a pelvis and machinery in Frida Kahlo's Henry Ford Hospital. In a 1935 painting, a white and yellow one of these things adorns a floating object against brown hills and a cloudy sky. A man on all fours uses a yellow ribbon to strap a heavy basket of these objects to his back in a Diego Rivera painting showing a (*) Carrier of these objects.The interpretation of paintings of these objects like Red Canna as stand-ins for female genitalia was rejected by an artist who created hundreds of paintings of these objects and animal skulls at her New Mexico studio. For 10 points, identify these colorful plant parts painted by Georgia O'Keeffe in works like Black Iris and Red Poppy.
2.r: flowers [accept oriental flowers; accept lilies; accept orchids; accept oriental poppies before mention]

2.q: This man painted an inverted clock falling out of the sky, a man being hanged, and another man stabbing a child, in a gouache painting in which Christ yells from the cross entitled Apocalypse in Lilac, Capriccio. He traveled to the Holy Land after Ambroise Vollard commissioned him to illustrate the Old Testament. He depicted scenes from 14 operas on a removable frame over Jules Eugene Lenepveu's original ceiling for the auditorium of the (*) Palais Garnier, the main opera house in Paris. This artist, many of whose paintings were inspired by his hometown of Vitebsk, painted a work showing tumbling houses and a burning synagogue surrounding Christ on the cross. For 10 points, name this Belarusian-born painter of White Crucifixion, who showed a green-faced man staring at a sheep in his painting I and the Village.

For over 40 years, many expansions of this institution were based on a master plan laid out by Kevin Roche. Calvert Vaux's red brick design for this institution was derided as a "mausoleum" and was replaced in a few years by Richard Morris Hunt's Beaux-Arts design. From 2015 to 2020, this institution operated a branch in a Marcel Breuer-designed building after The Whitney moved out. Fort Tryon Park is home to a (*) medieval-art-focused branch of this institution called the Cloisters. "Superfine" was the theme of the 2025 edition of this institution's annual gala organized by Anna Wintour. For 10 points, name this largest art museum in New York City.
2.r: Metropolitan Museum of Art [accept the Met; accept the Met Cloisters or the Met Breuer]

2.q: A complete set of these figures in soapstone, which adorns the Santuario do Bom Jesus de Matosinhos in Congonhas, is the magnum opus of the disfigured Brazilian mestizo sculptor Aleijadinho (ah-lay-hah-DEEN-yoh). The west facade of the Amiens cathedral contains sculptures of these figures, below each of which are two quatrefoil panels illustrating their lives. Twelve panels surrounding the center of the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel contain five ancient sibyls and seven of these biblical figures. While sculpting one of these figures, (*) Donatello apocryphally yelled "speak, damn you, speak!" at the marble. Donatello's sculpture of one of these figures has a bald head that earned it the nickname Zuccone. Habakkuk is one of, for 10 points, what set of twelve "minor" Old Testament figures who claimed to foretell the future?

For his third attempt to win the Prix de Rome, William Bouguereau submitted a painting inspired by this author that depicts a nude man biting another man's throat. A figure in a brown cloak steadies this author in a painting whose background depicts a burning city. That painting, which depicts this author cowering away from some figures chewing on a boat, is by Eugene (*) Delacroix. Three figures place their fists next to each other at the top of a bronze sculptural group inspired by this author that also depicts two figures embracing in The Kiss. This author rests his face on his fist in contemplation in the sculpture The Thinker. For 10 points, Auguste Rodin was inspired to create The Gates of Hell by what author's Divine Comedy?

This artist depicted a kneeling knight being crowned by a man who steps over a skeleton in a scene flanked by birth and baptism scenes. The inclusion of three Marys led to a dispute with one city's cathedral in a painting by this artist where the title figure's red robe is removed. Nude figures raise yellow and green cloths to the right of a blue-clad (*) St. John the Evangelist in a painting by this artist. This artist of The Disrobing of Christ also painted a row of noblemen standing behind the gold-clad St. Stephen and St. Augustine as they lower the title man into his tomb. For 10 points, name this Cretan-born painter of Opening of the Fifth Seal and The Burial of the Count of Orgaz.
2.r: El Greco [accept Doménikos Theotokópoulos] (the unnamed work is the Modena Triptych)

2.q: In a painting of one of these events, a man with an apparent extra foot walks by a nobleman talking to a grey-cloaked monk. Petrus Christus portrayed participants in one of these events in a painting once thought to depict St. Eligius. In the foreground of a painting of one of these events, a boy in a large cap with a peacock feather licks his finger. A painting titled for one of these events features details such as an orange on a (*) windowsill, two wooden clogs, and a little dog. Two men use a door to carry pudding towards a feast table in a painting of a "peasant" one of these events by Pieter Brueghel. A convex mirror appears below the artist's signature in a depiction of one of these events in which a man holds hands with woman in a green dress. For 10 points, name this type of event depicted by Jan van Eyck's Arnolfini Portrait.

A trompe-l'œil ["tromp loy"] tempera-on-plaster ceiling mural in this city simulates a canopy of mulberry trees. In this non-Rome city, Donato Bramante designed a false apse for the Church of Santa Maria presso San Satiro. Giovanni Antonio Amadeo decorated this city's Gothic main cathedral, where the tallest of 135 spires is topped with the golden (*) Madonnina. A mural in this city includes a man who knocked over a salt cellar while clutching a small bag. The central figure's feet in a mural were destroyed after a doorway was widened at the Santa Maria delle Grazie in this city. For 10 points, Leonardo da Vinci's The Last Supper was commissioned in what city by Ludovico Sforza?

Francisco de Zurburan painted several depictions of Saint Francis holding one of these objects while meditating. A painting dedicated to "all great conquerors, past, present, and future" depicting a massive number of these objects on top of each other was painted by Vasily Vereshchagin. One of these objects rests on a book across from a boy resting his elbow on another book in a still life by Paul (*) Cezanne, who also created a still life vanitas painting depicting four of these objects stacked on top of each other. Damien Hirst studded one of these with diamonds, and a very large anamorphic one is in the bottom-center of The Ambassadors. For 10 points, name these objects often used in paintings to show the fragile mortality of life.

Many of this artist's drawings and models were turned into sculptures by the Norwegian artist Carl Nesjar. The sci-fi author Algis Budrys placed a giant pickle on the future site of a sculpture by this artist. He made six versions, one of which incorporates a real spoon, of his bronze sculpture of an absinthe glass. He also made a bronze sculpture of a man holding a (*) lamb. This artist welded together a bicycle seat and handlebars to make his sculpture Bull's Head. He made cardboard and sheet metal versions of a sculpture of an instrument with its sound hole projecting outwards, his Guitar. People like to climb on a large sculpture by this artist in Daley Plaza, Chicago. His Head of a Woman is a bust of his lover, Dora Maar. For 10 points, name this co-founder, with Georges Braque, of cubism.

This artist painted himself staring at the viewer in a Gustave Dore-inspired painting that depicts prisoners walking in a circle in a courtyard. Francis Bacon created several versions of a self-portrait of this artist carrying an easel and walking on a road, called Painter on the Way to Work. In a self-portrait by this artist, the Japanese print Geishas in a Landscape hangs on the wall. In 2011, researchers determined that one of his self-portraits actually depicts his (*) brother Theo. One of this artist's self-portraits features him wearing a fur hat and smoking a pipe. This artist wears a straw hat in several of his self-portraits, while several others depict him with a bandage which he wore after cutting off part of his ear. For 10 points, name this Dutch artist of Starry Night.

An artist of this movement, derided by one contemporaneous critic as "capable of everything-except the truth," created a portrait of a woman in a green dress adorned with pink roses and bows. A woman holds a white dog with a blue-ribboned leash in one of several "Fantasy Figures" painted by an artist of this movement. Venetian artist Rosalba Carriera painted portraits identified with this movement. The back of a female sculpture appears behind a guitar-holding (*) Mezzetin in a painting of the stock commedia dell'arte character from this movement. Madame de Pompadour commissioned portraits from Francois Boucher, an artist of this movement. For 10 points, a man looks up the skirt of a woman on a swing in a Jean-Honore Fragonard painting exemplifying what highly ornamented movement?
2.r: Rococo [accept Late Baroque; do not accept or prompt on “Baroque”] (The critic in the first clue is Denis Diderot, and the painting mentioned is Boucher’s 1756 Portrait of Madame de Pompadour; Mezzetin was painted by Jean-Antoine Watteau.)

2.q: For the MoMA's Modern Restaurant, Mickalene Thomas reimagined one of these events with collaged images of three afroed black women. It's not an execution, but an artist cut into three pieces a painting of one of these events featuring Frederic Bazille. A painting of one of these events elicited the assertion that "no one goes to the Louvre to be scandalized" from Emile Zola. A brittle-boned artist repeatedly copies a painting of one of these events in the film (*) Amelie. A painting of one of these events drew poses from Marcantonio Raimondi's Judgement of Paris. Aline Charigot plays with a dog while guests in straw hats converse under a striped awning in a Renoir painting of one of these events. For 10 points, a nude woman sits with two fully-dressed men in a Manet painting of a gathering for what meal "on the grass?"
2.r: luncheons [or déjeuners or lunches; accept Luncheon on the Grass or Luncheon of the Boating Party; prompt on picnic or boating party by asking “For what meal?”] (The second clue refers to Monet’s Luncheon on the Grass.)

2.q: This artist often included diagonal stripes running down his subjects' faces in a series of 1980's works on painted bronze, called Expressionist Head. His portrait of Madame Cezanne is actually just a diagram with labels using letters of the alphabet. He used oil and Magna paint in his version of Bedroom at Arles, which includes Mies van der Rohe- inspired chairs and a green and white floor. Exhausted soldiers with fungal infections are the subject of his (*) Takka Takka. His series The Artist's Studio features a dumbass saying "I've hooked a big one!" Another painting by this artist of Look Mickey! features the text "I pressed the fire control... and ahead of me rockets blazed through the sky..." For 10 points, name this user of Ben Day dots, a pop artist who created Whaam!

Six of these objects rest on a floor made of broken glass in a "De-Coll/age" by Wolf Vostell. This object is the first word in a Chris Burden performance piece where he holds Phyllis Lutjeans at knife point. One artist's earlier work Global Groove was used in the installation of a "garden" of these objects. Three of these items are stacked into a cello that was played by Charlotte Moorman, who also wore two of these items as a (*) bra for one performance. A series by one artist features a statue of the Buddha facing this object, as a camera fixates on the face of the statue. Neon lights create a map of America in front of 336 of these objects in Electronic Superhighway, a work of Nam June Paik. For 10 points, what common household electronics are often used in video installation art?
2.c: 2020 Michigan Winter Tournament Pkt Tiebreakers_Extras Q3

2.q: This artist's first marble depicts an angel with some of her bones and internal organs exposed. A painting by this artist was cut into 88 pieces and auctioned off by the art collective MSCHF ("mischief"). The Utopia Art Colony accused this artist of appropriating the Australian Aboriginal practice of dot painting for his "Veil Paintings." Artworks from this artist's In and Out of Love compendium employ dead (*) butterflies as a material. This artist arranged emojis of pregnant women in a 4-by-3 array for the cover of a 2021 Drake album. This artist encrusted over 8,000 diamonds onto a platinum cast to create a crystal skull sculpture titled For the Love of God. For 10 points, an installation by what former Young British Artist consists of a tiger shark preserved in formaldehyde?
2.r: Damien Hirst [or Damien Steven Hirst or Damien Steven Brennan] (The sculpture in the first line is Anatomy of an Angel.)

2.q: Tony Vaccaro ("vah-KAR-roh") twice photographed this non-Alexander Calder artist posing outdoors with a yellow and red painting and holding a piece of cheese inside a car. A yellow line bisects rows of gray hills described as a "mile of elephants" in a subset of desolate landscapes by this artist. Airplane trips taken by this artist of the Pelvis Series inspired a series of minimalist paintings depicting the Sky Above Clouds. This artist painted The (*) Black Place at least five times while staying at the Ghost Ranch. A desert landscape is the backdrop of many of this artist's paintings of floating animal skulls. For 10 points, name this artist who gradually stopped creating up-close paintings of flowers, such as Red Canna and Jimson Weed, after moving to New Mexico.

Three figures representing justice, temperance, and fortitude overlook an enclosed garden from a circular cloud in the upper-right of this artist's Triumph of the Virtues. A potted plant rests precariously on a thin bar in another work by this artist that also features several portraits of Roman emperors on its roundels. Four Corinthian columns divide three scenes connected by hanging garlands in this artist's Saint Zeno Altarpiece. Anachronistic Roman ruins are visible behind a contrapposto figure (*) tied to a column and pierced by arrows in another work by this artist. The central figure's hands and feet are propped up to show his wounds while resting on a marble slab in an extremely foreshortened work by this artist. For 10 points, name this Mantuan artist of St. Sebastian and The Dead Christ.

A depiction of this figure in the Sassetti Chapel stands on a pedestal reading "saluti patriae et Christianae gloriae." Maffeo Barberini sponsored the creation of a depiction of this figure that unusually features a harp at his feet and bites its lip as it twists to the right away from the viewer. Verrocchio's depiction of this figure rests his left hand on his hip and has (*) flowers covering his nipples. Another depiction of this figure in the Bargello rests on a sword and was the first freestanding bronze statue made during the Renaissance. The Galleria dell'Accademia is home to an upright depiction of this figure that holds a slingshot over its shoulder. For 10 points, name this Biblical figure depicted in statues by Donatello and Michelangelo, in which he stands above the head of the slain Goliath.
2.c: 2015 STIMPY Pkt 02. Columbia A - WKU A Q11

2.q: This artist may have showed his mistress clutching her left breast in a portrait to cover a tumor. He borrowed from the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel to paint The Prophet Isaiah for an altar dedicated to Saint Anne. Two angels carry chalices with Christ's blood in a crucifixion by this artist of La Fornarina, who used a green curtain to frame a painting of two cherubs staring up at the Virgin. A Madonna by this artist of the (*) Mond Crucifixion and Sistine Madonna shows the infant Christ reaching out to pet a small bird held by John the Baptist. An elderly man points upwards while holding Timaeus with his left hand in one of this artist's paintings from the Stanza della Segnatura [sen-ya-TOO-rah]. For 10 points, name this painter of the Madonna of the Goldfinch, and The School of Athens.

Manny Farber's essay "White Elephant Art versus Termite Art" analyzes works in this medium. James Baldwin's 1976 book The Devil Finds Work also analyzes works in this medium. British academic Laura Mulvey analyzed the idea of "visual pleasure" in this medium, arguing that works in it are oriented to please the (*) "male gaze." The term "neorealism" is used to describe works in this medium made in Italy immediately after World War II, such as Rome, Open City and Bicycle Thieves. For 10 points, what medium is known for works by people like Christopher Nolan and Steven Spielberg?

A basalt stele(STEE-lee) depicts this city's ruler standing before a seated god of the sun. This city was home to a statue of a saddled lion trampling a human. A building in this city is decorated with walking aurochs and mushussu(mush-kush-shu) dragons, and stands at the end of a half-mile Processional Way. That building, which lay at one of the entrances to a "neo"-version of this city, was the (*) Ishtar Gate. The attempted construction of a tower to Heaven in this city is recounted in Christian mythology as the reason people speak different languages. For 10 points, name this city that was home to King Nebuchadnezzar II's Hanging Gardens.
2.r: Babylon [or Babel or Neo-Babylon; accept the Babylonian Empire, Neo-Babylonian Empire, or Second Babylonian Empire]

2.q: One of these objects and its user are the main subjects of the Alexamenos graffito, which contains the oldest visual depiction of these objects. The oldest of these objects in sculpture from north of the Alps was constructed around 965 AD and is named for Gero, while another sculpture of one named for Lothair is a prime example of Ottonian art. They were displayed in gemmata form prior to the Middle Ages due to a belief that their "glorified" version was more appropriate for the public eye. One of them is at the center of the best known painting of (*) Rogier van der Weyden. Andreas Serrano's most controversial work shows one submerged in urine. Two thieves are shown on these objects in many paintings set at Calvary. For 10 points, identify this object used by the Romans to kill Jesus.

This artist painted a mustachioed man in a black and gold helmet and blue loincloth with armor at his feet in Mars Resting. In another work by this artist, a man hands a boy a glass of water while another boy drinks in the shadows. A shirtless man with grape-leaves in his hair reclines on a wine barrel while a kneeling man is crowned during a drunken feast by the title figure in this artist's Triumph of (*) Bacchus. A man in a pink sash places his hand on Justin of Nassau's shoulder in this artist's painting The Surrender at Breda. Francis Bacon distorted this man's portrait of Pope Innocent X. This artist's only double portrait of a certain king and queen appears can be seen in the mirror of another work by him depicting ladies-in-waiting at the Alcazar palace attending to the Infanta Margarita. For 10 points, name this court painter for Philip IV of Spain and artist of Las Meninas.

A significant number of artworks from this non-French country were destroyed in the 2004 Momart fire destroyed. Yuan Chai and Jian Jun Xi [jyen jwin shee] jumped around on an artwork from this country before having a 15-minute pillow fight on top of it; the same artist from here created a tent with the names of "Everyone I Have Ever Slept With: 1963-1995." Tracey Emin works in this country. Former ad mogul (*) Charles Saatchi collects works primarily made by artists from here. An artist from this country sparked the Stuckist movement in his work The Physical Impossibility of Death in the Mind of Someone Living, which shows a tiger shark preserved in a vat of formaldehyde. For 10 points, name this home of Damien Hirst, whose namesake "Young Artists" sometimes exhibit at the Tate Modern.
2.r: the United Kingdom [accept Great Britain, the UK, GB; accept England as well, since all the artists talked about are specifically English]

2.q: Four women use a sheet to bounce a man-sized doll into the air in this artist's painting The Straw Manikin. A portrait of this artist's one time lover depicts her pointing to his initials drawn in the sand in front of her and is usually titled The Black Duchess. A off-balance man vomits onto a pile of bodies in this artist's This is What You Were Born For, part of his series of 82 prints called (*) Disasters of War. Another series of prints by this artist frequently depicts anthropomorphic donkeys. This artist of Los Caprichos depicted a goat-headed demon lording over a witch gathering and a wild-eyed Titan holding his half-consumed offspring in his most famous series. For 10 points, name this Spanish artist whose Black Paintings includes Saturn Devouring his Son
2.r: Francisco Goya [accept Francisco Jose de Goya y Lucientes]
2.c: 2019 Florida Spring Tournament (FST) Pkt D. Packet 4 Q13

2.q: This artist's work was championed by Thomas B. Hess, who outlined his process in the article "[this artist] Paints a Picture." A portrait sometimes thought to depict this artist, which probably actually depicts a Swedish carpenter, shows its subject holding a palette in his lap. Though primarily known as a painter, he also made sculptures such as Clamdigger and Seated Woman on a Bench. Robert (*) Rauschenberg erased one of this artist's drawings. This friend of Arshile Gorky married Elaine Fried. Between 1950 and 1953, he made a series of paintings including one which pairs its central figure with a bicycle. For 10 points, name this Dutch-American painter of the Woman series.

A red-cloaked angel swings a censer toward a glowing triangle in this man's extremely orange fresco Adoration of the Name of the Lord. A woman leans on what may be a burial mound topped by wrought-iron rails in a probable portrait of this man's maid Leocadia, while a woman holding a striped box sits apart from a semicircle gathered around a goat-headed man in another of his paintings. Horses trample people and men fight with daggers and curved swords in a painting by this artist of The (*) Witches' Sabbath that served as a companion to a work in which a square lantern illuminates two opposing lines of people and a white-shirted man throws up his hands. A bloody, headless man is being eaten in one of this man's Black Paintings. For 10 points, name this Spanish painter of Saturn Devouring His Son and The Third of May, 1808.
2.r: Francisco Goya [or Francisco José de Goya y Lucientes]

2.q: Pieter Claesz [class], a prominent painter of works in this genre, specialized in a type of them called bedriegertje [beh-DREE-gur-cheh] or "deceptive." Some members of Les Nabis [lay nah-bee] crowd around a painting in this genre in an "homage" by Maurice Denis. This genre was placed last in the 18th-century "hierarchy of painting," which placed history painting at the top. Francisco Zurbaran painted numerous examples of a Spanish variant of these artworks known as a (*) bodegon [boh-day-GOHN]. Examples of these works that depict themes of death are called vanitas examples and often contain skulls. Paul Cezanne's approach to these works can be seen in paintings such as his Basket of Apples. For 10 points, identify these works that depict inanimate objects.

Art historian Wilhelm Fraenger ("VIL-helm FRENG-er") controversially claimed that this work was created to endorse the Adamites. A scene in this painting shows God in pink robes handing Eve to Adam, who stares at her lustfully. Building-sized musical instruments appear on this painting's right, earning that section the nickname "The Musicians' Hell." The outer panels of this triptych ("TRIP-tick") are thought to depict the third day of the Creation. This painting's right panel features a (*) "Tree Man" in front of a large pair of ears carrying a knife. Its middle panel depicts countless nude figures cavorting with oversized animals and fruits. For 10 points, name this insane triptych depicting humanity giving into sin and being punished in hell, the magnum opus of Hieronymus Bosch ("high-RON-a-muss BOSH")

A red border surrounds an artwork from this city depicting Cupid and Psyche making and smelling perfume. Intuitive perspective is employed in many Second Style works defined by paintings from this city that depict various initiation rites. "Obscene" artworks from this city, including a statuette of Venus in a "gold bikini," comprise most of the items exhibited in the Secret Room. A general wears a medusa-emblemed breastplate in a ruined floor (*) mosaic from this city commemorating Alexander the Great's victory at the Battle of Issus. Intact wall frescoes can still be found in many of this city's well-preserved domus estates, such as the House of the Faun. For 10 points, what Roman city's artworks became buried after the eruption of Mount Vesuvius?

This building contains a line of paired panels of painted marble decorations interspersed with grisaille paintings of the Vices and Virtues. Two angels push out portions of the sky above a window that is also flanked by massed ranks of angels in a painting in this building, which also contains a painting in which a man's ear is severed as a yellow- robed Judas dramatically comes face-to-face with Jesus. Ten angels dart about the sky of a depiction of the (*) Lamentation in this building. Its star-studded cobalt blue ceiling is located above rows of paintings depicting the lives of Joachim, Christ, and the Virgin. Its entire west wall is covered by a painting of The Last Judgement, in which small model of this building is presented to the Virgin by its patron, Enrico Scrovegni. For 10 points, name this church in Padua home to a famous fresco cycle by Giotto.
2.r: the Arena Chapel [accept the Scrovegni Chapel or the Cappella degli Scrovegni before “Scrovegni” is read]

2.q: The Toledo Museum of Art is home to a massive black steel geometric sculpture by Tony Smith with this name. This name ends the title of a hexagonal sculpture depicting a ring of six men and a now-lost crucifixion scene found in Chartreuse de Champmol. That sculpture, created for John the Fearless, is a "Well of" this name designed by Claus Sluter. An artist with this surname depicted oxen pulling timber-filled sleighs, a roiling black cauldron on a huge fire, and people pouring (*) maple syrup onto snow in the painting Sugaring Off. A sculpture of a man with this name intended for the tomb of Pope Julius II was based on a description from the Vulgate, explaining that man's unusually horned head. For 10 points, give the name shared the Old Testament figure depicted in that Michelangelo sculpture and by a painter known as "Grandma".
2.c: 2014 Minnesota Undergraduate Tournament (MUT) Pkt Finals 2 Q8

2.q: Spirals permeate the set of the only surviving film from this artistic movement, Thais. Several paintings of the Brooklyn Bridge and Coney Island were created by an American member of this art movement, Joseph Stella. After leaving the group Donkey's Tail, two artists founded a Russian offshoot of this movement, (*) Rayonism. Multiple artists in this movement painted works showing simultaneous views of moving objects like a cyclist and a dog on a leash, each titled for their subject's Dynamism. The manifesto for this art movement called for a rapid modernization of the country of its author, Filippo Marinetti. For 10 points, name this early 20th century Italian art movement of Luigi Russolo and Umberto Boccioni that glorified violence, speed, and modern technology.

Ross Cramer designed an artwork in this medium that shows a man with a bulging stomach and asks "Would you be more careful if it was you that got pregnant?" Another of these artworks prominently displays the word SOLD beneath Honest Gil Fulbright. A black-and-white photo of a model's face is split into halves of positive and negative exposure in one of these artworks created by Barbara Kruger that displays the words "your (*) body is a battleground." In 2008, the activist who founded OBEY clothing created one of these artworks in red, white, and blue whose variants showed the words "progress" and "change" under the face of a then-Senator from Illinois. For 10 points, give this sort of artwork exemplified by Shephard Fairey's iconic piece that shows the word "HOPE" next to Barack Obama's face.
2.r: posters [accept political posters or campaign posters; prompt on ads or advertisements or political ads or prints or screen prints or graphics]

2.q: In 2006, a one-eyed artist who works in this medium sued Robert Kaindl and Bryan Rubino for copyright. After The Slav Epic, an artwork in this medium that depicts a boy St. Wenceslas and the life of St. Cyril was created in Prague by Alphonse Mucha. The Curtis Publishing Company commissioned Maxfield Parrish for an artwork in this medium titled Dream Garden. It's not light, but a craftsman called a gaffer leads the production of this medium, which was used for the "Seaform" and (*) "Venetian" series. Duchamp wrote The Green Box notes for an artwork subtitled The Large [this medium]. Dale Chihuly works in this medium, whose "favrile" type appears in Tiffany lamps. For 10 points, name this medium shaped by namesake "blowing," and is colored to create its "stained" form.
2.r: glass [accept stained glass or favrile glass; accept glassblowing; accept The Large Glass; prompt on mural]

2.q: One painting by this artist inspired a photograph in which leaves from two dead trees and paper thrown into the air are caught by the title Sudden Gust of Wind. In that original painting by this artist, two men clutch their hats while a third man watches his trilby blow away. In another work by this artist, three men camp alongside the banks of a waterfall emerging from a circular cliffside opening. According to legend, this artist chased a (*) chicken with red paint on its feet across a canvas to create one landscape. An elderly cooper constructs an unusually large barrel in the foreground of another painting by this artist. Small boats are threatened by the title force of nature with Mount Fuji in the background in this artist's best-known work. For 10 points, name this Japanese ukiyo-e ("YOO-kee-OH-ey") printmaker of Great Wave of Kanagawa.
2.r: Katsushika Hokusai (the unnamed Hokusai works in power are Travellers Caught in a Sudden Breeze at Ejiri and The Waterfall of Amida behind the Kiso Road)

2.q: The spies of Eshcol and the Three Magi are shown in the detailed border of a work partially titled for this phrase, which derives from the last stanza of a George Berkley poem. In that work, two men raise the American flag atop a rock formation. Another work titled for this phrase depicts an old man drawing geometric figures with a stick, while trees obscure smoke coming from a stone temple. A headless statue posed like the (*) Borghese Gladiator features in a series titled for this phrase, whose last entry shows birds nesting on an overgrown column. A mural in the Capitol painted by Emanuel Leutze is titled for how "Westward [this phrase] Takes Its Way." For 10 points, name this phrase that titles a series about the rise and fall of civilization by Thomas Cole.
2.r: The Course of Empire [accept Westward The Course of Empire Takes Its Way; prompt on Westward Ho by asking “What is the more common name for that painting?”]

2.q: An artist with this surname was inspired by a statue in the Luxembourg Gardens to create a series of paintings depicting Bacchus. Cathy Curtis's book A Generous Vision describes an artist with this surname's creation of a series of paintings inspired by Paleolithic cave paintings. An artist with this surname is called An American Master in the subtitle of a Mark Stevens and Annalyn Swan biography and created the lumpy bronze sculpture Clamdigger. An artist with this surname exhibited a series of abstract black-and-white paintings at the Charles Egan gallery. Robert (*) Rauschenberg created an artwork by erasing a drawing by an artist with this surname who painted the colorful Woman series. For 10 points, give this surname of the Dutch-American Abstract Expressionist artist Willem.
2.r: de Kooning [or Willem de Kooning; or Elaine de Kooning; accept Elaine Fried UNTIL “An American Master” is read and PROMPT afterwards]

2.q: These objects are the defining features of three figures who stand at different angles under crescent moons in the painting The Mysteries of the Horizon. In a late painting by one artist, the silhouette of a man wearing one of these objects 'cuts out' a section of red curtain through which the sea can be seen. In a painting of 1964, a white dove flies directly in front of the face of a man wearing one of these items. A large green (*) apple obscures the face of a man wearing one of these objects in the painting The Son of Man. People wearing these objects appear to fall from the sky in the painting Golconda. For 10 points, Rene Magritte often painted figures wearing a suit with what other item of clothing on their heads?
2.r: hats [accept any type of hats, such as bowler hats; prompt on suits with “What other items of clothing are the subjects wearing?”]

2.q: Photographer David Butcher was commissioned in 2017 to take a series landscape photographs of the rocky coastlines of Cap de Creus that inspired this painter. This artist's villa at Port Lligat ("poor LEE-gah") included sculptures of an egg balance on a rooftop and a cyprus growing from a boat. A Florida museum dedicated to this artist's works houses several of his large canvases like The (*) Ecumenical Council and The Discovery of America by Christopher Columbus. The atomic bomb inspired this artist's late in life shift to the style of "nuclear mysticism," though he is better known for a style exemplified by works like The Great Masturbator and Swans Reflecting Elephants. For 10 points, name this Spanish surrealist who painted melting clocks in The Persistence of Memory.
2.c: 2019 Florida Spring Tournament (FST) Pkt K. Packet 11 Q8

2.q: An Ottawa location of this type includes a staircase into a distorted doorway near a triangular "Sky Void." Concrete "books" line the exterior of one of these places designed by Rachel Whiteread in Vienna. Christine Jacob-Marks included a 100 meter by 100 meter plan for her design of another of these places that was vetoed in favor of a collaboration between Richard Serra and Peter (*) Eisenman, whose design consists of 2,711 concrete slabs that visitors pass through. Brass plates known as "stumbling stones" are often seen in these places. One of these places in Skokie, Illinois was the world's first to incorporate holograms with the help of Yad Vashem. For 10 points, name these places which serve as reminders to a Nazi-perpetrated genocide.

In one painting set in this city, an inscription above a brick archway beckons those who "wish to repair to patience and meekness" with the proverb that "we must first descend if we wish to be raised". That painting in this city, in which a broom lays in front of a bucket in front of a woman in blue holding the hand of a little girl in yellow, is titled for the "courtyard of a house" in this city, which is the setting of another painter's The Little Street. The painter of The Goldfinch, Carel (*) Fabritius, was a member of a school of genre painters based in this city. Two women wearing shawls are separated from two herring boats and the Neuwe Kirk [NOO-wuh "Kirk"] by the Schie ["ski"] canal in a painting of this city's skyline by the artist of The Astronomer and Girl With a Pearl Earring. For 10 points, name this hometown of Jan Vermeer, who painted a "view of" this Dutch city.
2.r: Delft [accept The Courtyard of a House in Delft or Delft School or View of Delft]

2.q: A painting by Judith Leyster ("YOU-dit LICE-ter") in this genre includes a laughing violinist dressed in blue. One work in this genre depicts a jaundiced god holding grapes and is titled Young Sick Bacchus. Another painting in this genre is subtitled "the Allegory of Painting". A painting thought to be in this genre by Artemisia Gentileschi ("jent-uh-LESS-key") shows a woman in blue beheading a man who possibly depicts Agostino Tassi. (*) Saskia is included in many works of this type by Rembrandt. A painting in this genre that depicts a man with a green overcoat and bandaged ear was created by Vincent van Gogh using a mirror. For 10 points, name this genre of painting in which an artist depicts themself.
2.r: self-portraits [accept Self-Portrait as the Allegory of Painting or Autoritratto in veste di Pittura; accept Self-Portrait as Bacchus; accept Self-Portrait with Bandaged Ear; prompt on double portraits; prompt on history paintings by asking “What other genre is that painting thought to be in?”]

2.q: In one scene by this artist set in the countryside, a pig and a horse are seen grazing in the background as his wife wearing a blue shirt lies on the ground. In addition to The Poet Reclining, this artist depicted himself in a red jacket holding a wine glass sitting on his lover's shoulders in a double portrait. On the left of one painting, this artist included black-clad troops carrying weapons and a red flag. The right side of that painting shows a (*) Lithuanian flag behind a burning place of worship. This artist's portraits often included his wife Bella Rosenfeld, who was also born in Vitebsk. He included two upside down houses, a woman milking a goat, and large green face with white lips in his masterpiece. For 10 points, name this Belarusian artist of The White Crucifixion and I and the Village.

A portrait by this painter shows its subject holding a toy airplane while both the sun and the moon are present in the sky to her left and right. Another portrait by this artist shows its subject covered in nails and with a fissure-like split torse within which a doric column appears. This artist depicted a volcano, a building, and plants emerging from tub water in (*) What the Water Gave Me. Another painting by this artist shows its subject flanked by a black monkey and black cat while a dead hummingbird hangs from her neck. A historic museum dedicated to this artist's life and work is housed in her long-time home, a cobalt-colored house known as La Casa Azul. For 10 points, name this unibrow-sporting Mexican artist known for her surrealist self-portraits.
2.r: Frida Kahlo [accept Frida Kahlo de Rivera; accept Magdalena Carmen Frida Kahlo y Calderón]
2.c: 2019 Florida Spring Tournament (FST) Pkt F. Packet 6 Q18

2.q: One of these animals covers a model's genitals in a costume for the funhouse Dream of Venus. An artist was allegedly stopped from adding mayonnaise to an outfit printed with sprigs of parsley and one of these animals. Cecil Beaton took pre-wedding photos of Wallis Simpson in a dress that depicted one of these animals and was created by Elsa Schiaparelli. One artist questioned why he could ask for a grilled one of these animals, but not a particular (*) electronic device. A plaster one of these animals adorns the mouthpiece of a telephone created by Salvador Dali. This is the first of two animals that title a steel wire and sheet aluminum sculpture that hangs in the MoMA stairwell. For 10 points, a trap for what animal is paired with a Fish Tail in the title of a mobile by Alexander Calder?
2.r: lobsters [accept Lobster Dress; or Lobster Telephone; or Lobster Trap and Fish Tail]

2.q: This city is home to Fountain of Time, which commemorates peace between the US and UK, and a Yoko Ono sculpture of steel lotus petals titled Skylanding. An installation in this city consists of a granite pool fed by two glass-brick towers that display videos of faces. A vague skull or mushroom cloud shape is contained in a Henry Moore sculpture in this city commemorating the first (*) nuclear reactor. The sculptures Nuclear Energy and Flamingo are located in this city, as is an Anish Kapoor sculpture inspired by the flow of liquid mercury. The paintings Nighthawks and American Gothic are located in this city's Art Institute. For 10 points, Cloud Gate, nicknamed "The Bean," is located in what Midwestern city?

Pierre-Auguste Renoir described a statue of this figure as a "big gendarme," while another sculpture of this figure is depicted on the right of Johan Zoffany's The Tribuna of the Uffizi. A statue of this figure in the pudica stance named for Filippo Giueseppe Colonna was donated to the Vatican Museums. Another sculpture of this figure was commissioned by Camillo Borghese and depicts a member of the (*) Bonaparte family. Another sculpture of this figure is depicted multiple times in Salvador Dali's The Hallucinogenic Toreador. The first full-size female nude was designed by Praxiteles for this deity's temple at Knidos. For 10 points, name this Greco-Roman goddess of love depicted in an unarmed statue from Melos.

A work by this artist was originally enclosed in an oblong box topped by a salamander, one of which he claimed to have seen in a fireplace at the age of five. One of this artist's sculptures has a base depicting the four seasons and the four parts of the day. A lunette by this artist features hounds flanking a reclining nymph with her arm around a deer. He used bed sheets to escape from the Castel Sant'Angelo, an episode (*) featured in a text that narrates his sculpting of a piece in which blood drips from a disembodied head. This artist of The Nymph of Fontainebleau described in his Autobiography how he "represented the Sea and the Land, both seated, with their legs intertwined" in a small gold piece for his patron Francis I. For 10 points, name this Renaissance artist of Perseus with the Head of Medusa and a Salt Cellar.

A pink bird and several of these animals gather around a dark woman with glowing eyes in an Henri Rousseau painting with a solitary full moon at the top left. The pose of a reclining nude's legs is mimicked by a pink one of these animals found to the right of two lions in another Rousseau painting, titled The Dream. A tiled blue wall decorated with calligraphy forms the background of a painting in which a nude boy with his back to the viewer holds two of these animals. That painting by (*) Jean-Leon Gerome ("zhay-ROME") titled for these animals is on the original cover of Edward Said's ("sa-EED's") Orientalism. The ouroboros ("yur-uh-BOR-us") symbol shows one of these animals, which feature in most scenes of The Death of Cleopatra. For 10 points, what kind of animal has an apple in its mouth in Henri Rousseau's Eve?
2.r: snake [accept serpent; accept specific varieties such as pythons or cobras or asps]

2.q: After visiting this artist in his studio, sculptor David d'Angers said "Here is a man who has discovered the tragedy of landscape." The title object is centered between a pair of figures who converse at twilight and a tree tilted at a sharp angle in this artist's Two Men Contemplating the Moon. In another painting, he depicted himself as an old man in a fur coat with a walking stick standing next to an overturned rowboat. This artist's brother drowned at age 13 while trying to save him after he fell through (*) ice, inspiring a recurring image of his, such as a painting in which a ship is caught in an iceberg. This artist allegorized aging by showing five ships at varying distances in another painting. This artist of The Sea of Ice and The Stages of Life painted a man with his back facing the viewer standing on a rock and staring into mist. For 10 points, name this Romantic painter of Wanderer Above the Sea of Fog.

A large entirely monochrome painting by this artist in the National Gallery depicts Cybele's introduction to Scipius Africanus. Jesus and the Virgin Mary are surrounded by thirteen disembodied figures in this artist's Madonna of the Cherubim. This artist decorated the roof of the Ducal Palace of Mantua with illusionistic frescoes, including one of a peacock surrounded by putti. This artist used his "agony in the garden" motif in his (*) San Zeno Altarpiece. Mirroring a work by Bellini, this artist depicted the title figure standing in front of a crumbling pillar and impaled by arrows in a trio of paintings depicting the sufferings of Saint Sebastian. A work by this artist places the viewer at the feet of Jesus's corpse as it lays upon a marble slab. For 10 points, name this Italian Renaissance artist who used foreshortening and perspective in his Lamentation of the Dead Christ.

Barbara Deimling asserted that this painting once hung directly to the right of one in which a woman carrying a halberd pulls the hair of a bow-wielding centaur. On the far left side of this painting, a male figure wearing a flame-bedecked red cloak who may have been modeled on Lorenzo di Pierfrancesco de' Medici points at a small patch of clouds with his caduceus. This painting also contains a woman in a diaphanous gown with (*) flowers falling out of her mouth who is the target of a swooping blue winged figure. In addition to those depictions of Chloris and Zephyrus, this painting features Cupid pointing his arrow at three intertwined dancing women. For 10 points, name this painting that depicts Mercury, the Graces, and Venus in an orange grove, a work of Botticelli that is also known as Allegory of Spring.
2.r: Primavera [accept Allegory of Spring before it is read; prompt on “Spring”]

2.q: This artist expressed disgust at a portrait by stating "I don't want anyone to know I posed for it." On a trip to Seville, this one-time student of Jean Leon Gerome depicted a toreador resting his muleta on a stick and smoking a cigarette in After the Bullfight. This artist's sister Lydia often appears, along with other women, holding a fan or wearing opera glasses in various scenes set at loges and theaters. This artist's study of Japanese prints shows in aquatints like (*) The Letter, as well as a work depicting a woman wearing stripes cleaning an infant's feet in water. She studied art and collaborated with Edgar Degas and various fellow Impressionists whom she helped popularize in her home country. For 10 points, name this artist of The Child's Bath, a woman born in the U.S.

A small one of these objects sits atop an elephant in a sculpture in the Piazza della Minerva that inspired figures in several Dali paintings. One of these objects was installed by Domenico Fontana 100 years before an architect surrounded it with extended, curving colonnades in a design for a square. One of these objects that is topped by a Pamphili emblem stands in the (*) Piazza Navona. That object sits above gods representing the Nile, Ganges, Danube, and Rio de la Plata in the Fountain of the Four Rivers by Bernini. Along with columns, many of these tall structures were brought to Rome from temples in Heliopolis and Karnak. For 10 points, name these ancient Egyptian stone towers whose modern day equivalents include the Washington Monument.
2.r: obelisks [prompt on fountains by asking “what kind of object is included in the fountain design?”]

2.q: One woman with a straw hat in this painting leans on a diagonal rail while staring at a man and the left side of this painting. Another woman, the future wife of the artist, on the left side of this painting has a flower in her hat and appears holding a dog in her arms. This painting shows its artist's patron Gustave (*) Caillebotte ("kai"-bot) in the lower right in a straw hat and a sleeveless shirt. The people depicted in this painting enjoy wine and food underneath a red and white awning while at the Maison Fournaise (for-nezz) restaurant. For 10 points, identify this Pierre-August Renoir painting which shows a group eating a meal next to the Seine.
2.r: Luncheon of the Boating Party [or Le déjeuner des canotier]

2.q: Note to players: Description acceptable. In one painting, a man performing this action glances over his shoulder at the viewer in front of a woman pouring a drink. Georges de La Tour made a second version of that painting in which the title object was changed to alter the symbolism of performing this action. In another painting, two men can be seen performing this action next to a group of men playing (*) dice. That painting took inspiration from another painting depicting this action, in which a man with fingerless gloves stands behind an oblivious boy. This action was famously depicted in a scene in which a boy with a knife holds his hand behind his back while playing primero, an early version of poker. For 10 points, what action can be seen in Caravaggio's The Cardsharps?
2.r: cheating at a game of cards [prompt on playing cards; prompt on gambling]

2.q: Castilian sculptures of this scene include a set of five by Gregorio Fernandez, one of which is also called Sexta Angustia. A sculpture of this scene in St. Peter's Basilica is the only sculpture signed by its artist, who wanted to dispel rumors that it was made by Cristoforo Solari. A sculpture of this scene commissioned by Jean Bilheres de Lagraulas shows one figure as impossibly (*) young, which its artist justified by saying chaste women age slower. A depiction of this scene by El Greco depicts the central male figure with his arms curled around two people in yellow and green shirts, while a blue-veiled woman gazes up at the sky behind him. Along with the Mater Dolorosa and the Stabat Mater, this is one of three common depictions of the Virgin Mary. For 10 points, name this scene that depicts Mary cradling the body of the dead Jesus, the subject of a sculpture by Michelangelo.
2.r: the Pieta [accept the Lamentation of Christ or Sorrow of the Virgin Mary; prompt on the Deposition or the Descent from the Cross]

2.q: A bunch of blue diagonal lines pierce passengers in one entry in a triptych from this art movement set at a train station. A Precisionist artist from this movement who immigrated to the US created several paintings that show gray, metallic cityscapes through the arches of the Brooklyn Bridge. An artist from this movement painted the States of Mind triptych and acted on his desire to separate from "analytical discontinuity" by creating a sculpture that uses two separate blocks as (*) pedestals for a figure modeled on the Nike of Samothrace. The feet of a dachshund are blurred in painting from this movement titled Dynamism of a Dog on a Leash by Giacomo Balla. The sculpture Unique Forms of Continuity in Space is from, for 10 points, what mostly Italian art movement that celebrated war and technology?
2.r: Futurism [or Futurismo] (The first clue refers to the painting Those Who Go.)

2.q: In one of this artist's works inspired by Steve Roper, a man swings open a peephole to scan a dark room only to discover nobody is in it. Erle Loran attempted to sue this artist over exhibiting life-size renditions of his black-and-white outline analyzing The Portrait of Madame Cezanne. A girl with blue hair closes her eyes as tears drip down her face in a work by this artist that shows the girl thinking "I don't care! I'd rather (*) sink than call Brad for help!" This artist of Drowning Girl used Ben-Day dots for his depiction of an anthropomorphic duck fishing and catching his own coat while a mouse laughs at his gaff. For 10 points, name this American pop artist whose comic-book style is seen in his works Look Mickey and Whaam!.

A painting that depicts Marcel Duchamp being photographed by Edward Steichen is titled for this time "in the Country" and was painted by Florine Stettheimer. After a 1985 earthquake, a work partly titled for this time was moved to a museum dedicated to it across from the park in which it was set. That mural anachronistically portrays Mexican historical figures and La Catrina and is (*) "Dream of" this time "in the Alameda Central" by Diego Rivera. A painting set during this time mirrors the artist's earlier Bathers at Asnieres by showing people including a woman with a leashed monkey along the Seine in a pointillist scene. For 10 points, Georges Seurat depicted Parisians relaxing on the Island of La Grande Jatte during what time period?
2.r: Sunday afternoon [prompt on partial answer; accept Sunday Afternoon in the Country; accept Dream of a Sunday Afternoon in the Alameda Central; accept A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte]

2.q: This artist is quoted as saying "You are interested in a certain painting because it is an arrangement of lines and colours" in "Vortex" by his admirer Ezra Pound. This artist depicted his patron as a bird playing piano in The Gold Scab after that patron, Frederick Leyland, sold off his property. His book The Gentle Art of Making Enemies was published with many of his butterfly monograms in its margins. This artist (*) won a single farthing in damages from a libel suit after he was accused of "flinging a pot of paint in the public's face" by John Ruskin. This artist delighted in irritating critics by giving his paintings musical titles such as Nocturne in Black and Gold. For 10 points, name this artist of Arrangement in Grey and Black, which depicts his mother.

An artist from this country often requested his sister Gerti to pose for his nude drawings. Another artist from this country painted himself sleeping with the widow of a composer in The Bride of the Wind. Chinese lantern plants frequently appear in ghastly portraits by an artist from this country, including one depicting his lover Wally Neuzil. After visiting Venice and Ravenna, an artist from this country embarked on a "phase" that saw him create paintings such as Hope II ("two"), (*) Danae, and Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I ("one"). This country's Belvedere houses a 1908 painting by one of its native sons depicting a couple embracing in front of a gold leaf field titled The Kiss. For 10 points, name this birth country of Egon Schiele and Gustav Klimt.
2.r: Austria [or Österreich; accept Austria-Hungary or Dual Monarchy; accept Republic of Austria; reject “Hungary”] (The first and third lines reference Egon Schiele. The second line references Oskar Kokoschka.)

2.q: A work by this artist inspired a still shot intercut with a crowd running from a nuclear meltdown in the 1990 film Dreams. Another work by this artist uses linear perspective via the outlines of planks behind an old cooper working inside his unfinished barrel. A line of men carrying red muskets and workers in a timberyard appear in two of the (*) ten extra works commissioned for one project by this artist. A depiction of a thunderstorm follows a work by this artist in which thin clouds on a Prussian blue sky appear to the left of the subject, bathed in red from the sunrise. That work, Fine Wind, Clear Morning, follows a piece by this artist that shows three barges struggling in a tsunami. For 10 points, The Great Wave off Kanagawa is from what artist's series Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji?
2.r: Katsushika Hokusai (Dreams was directed by Akira Kurosawa.)

2.q: A woman peels an orange and a toreador smokes a cigarette in two paintings this artist created in Seville. This artist curated Louisine Havemeyer's collection and depicted her in a white ball gown against a yellow background. Ludovic-Napoleon Lepic ["luh-peek"] gifted this artist a Brussels Griffon which was included in a turquoise-heavy painting of a young girl resting on an armchair. The Paris Salon accepted this artist's painting The Mandolin Player in 1868. Kitagawa (*) Utamaro's boudoir ukiyo-e woodprints inspired this artist's paintings of nude women changing such as The Toilette and The Coiffure. This artist leans on an umbrella and views Louvre paintings in a print series by her friend Edgar Degas ["day-gah"], whom she helped popularize in the US. For 10 points, name this Impressionist who often depicted mothers and children in paintings like The Child's Bath.
2.r: Mary Cassatt [or Mary Stevenson Cassatt] (The painting described in the third sentence is Little Girl in a Blue Armchair.)

2.q: In [emphasize] another artist's painting, this artist is depicted on the forehead of the central figure, whose lace and floral headpiece features web-like roots and strings extending to the edges of the canvas. This artist depicted himself as a child alongside his wife, who holds a yin-yang symbol in one work that centers on a floral hat and feathered rattlesnake boa-wearing (*) skeleton. This artist of Dream of a Sunday Afternoon in Alameda Central Park refused to remove a depiction of Vladimir Lenin, causing Nelson Rockefeller to order the destruction of his Man at the Crossroads. For 10 points, name this Mexican muralist and husband of Frida Kahlo.

In one painting from this movement, a large circular mirror sits behind an unfinished tapestry woven by a woman who is "Half-Sick of Shadows". In another painting from this movement, that red-haired woman sits on her tapestry in a black boat while floating down a forested river. Elizabeth (*) Siddal modeled for a painting from this movement that depicts a woman drowning in a river while holding flowers. That painting, Ophelia, was by a leading member of this movement, John Everett Millais ("MILL-ay"). For 10 points, name this British artistic movement named for rejecting the influence of a certain Italian painter.

A black horse charges at an oncoming train in a painting from this country. An Irish-born painter who worked in this country depicted the explorer John Henry Lefroy in The Surveyor. Another artist from this country painted billowing green trees surrounding a small white church in Yuquot ("YOU-kwot") Village. That artist was associated with a (*) group of painters which included A.Y. Jackson and Lawren Harris. That group from this country was heavily influenced by an artist who painted a green sky behind the title tree in The Jack Pine. For 10 points, name this home country of Tom Thomson, Emily Carr, and the Group of Seven.

A painting by this artist copies a portrait of Richard Wagner, as a man is seen on the left lifting a grand piano. A prominent red swastika armband is worn by a man near his horses in a winter landscape in this artist's Hitler Masturbating. Several copies of the Venus de Milo are seen under the face of this artist's wife (*) Gala in The Hallucinogenic Toreador, while in another painting, she is depicted as an array of spheres in the sky. Seeing a decomposing lizard as a child inspired this artist's motif of swarming ants, often seen as representing sexual anxiety. For 10 points, soft Camembert inspired what artist to paint melting watches in The Persistence of Memory?

While working with Jean-Michel Basquiat ("bas-key-at") this artist painted faces from Da Vinci's Last Supper onto a set of white punching bags. This artist's observation that "when you see a gruesome image over and over again, it really doesn't have any effect" inspired their series of prints depicting violent deaths and car crashes. Baby Jane Holzer was one of this artist's "superstars" who frequented their studio, which was nicknamed the (*) Factory for its "assembly line" to create silkscreens. This artist often filled canvases with repeated images, such as 50 copies of a movie star's face, or 32 objects with labels like "Clam Chowder" and "Chicken Noodle." For 10 points, name this pop artist who created the Marilyn Diptych and a series of paintings of Campbell's soup cans.

This artist depicted a young poet sitting at his desk while smoking a pipe in his Portrait of Baudelaire. A kneeling man in a yellow cap wielding a hammer is on the right side of a painting by this man which was destroyed during the Allied bombing of Dresden in World War II. Recently, scholars have debated whether a portrait of a young woman's head and shoulders by this artist was originally part of a painting of a nude woman's torso and (*) genitals. Another painting by this artist of The Origin of the World depicts a white dog in its foreground and a man dressed in white carrying a large crucifix in front of an open grave. For 10 points name this French Realist artist of The Stone Breakers and A Burial at Ornans.
2.c: 2018 Florida Spring Tournament (FST) Pkt K. Packet 11 Q1

2.q: This artist showed a woman holding one of her children while the other is perched atop a beached boat as they wait for their father in the painting Dad's Coming! In another of his paintings, a uniformed man defiantly standing with his right hand on his hip is at the head of a group of captured soldiers being looked upon by Francis Channing Barlow. He made several depictions of people playing croquet. This artist's A Visit from the (*) Old Mistress has a similar composition to a painting he made while working as a Civil War correspondent. This artist of Prisoners from the Front showed a man and three boys in a catboat called the Gloucester in his painting Breezing Up. In his best known work, sharks mass around a small fishing boat with a black man lying on the deck. For 10 points, name this painter of nautical scenes like The Gulf Stream.

Birth control pill inventor Carl Djerassi claimed that a work by this artist was a caricature of Hitler, pointing to this artist's lithograph The Angler. The undulating steel facade of a Renzo Piano-designed "Center" for this artist alludes to this artist's description of drawing as "taking an active line on a walk, moving freely." Georges Bataille, Theodor Adorno, and Gershom Scholem were sequentially entrusted with a work by this artist whose leery-eyed subject was analogized to history by (*) Walter Benjamin. This artist's 1914 visit to Tunisia inspired his move to abstract color painting and his large pointillist work ad Parnassum. A watercolor by this Bauhaus artist depicts a crank connected to a wire holding four stick-figure birds. For 10 points, name this Swiss-German artist of Angelus Novus and Twittering Machine.
2.r: Paul Klee (The first sentence refers to Angelus Novus.)

2.q: After this artist appeared in the music video for "Rapture" by Blondie, Debbie Harry bought his painting Cadillac Moon for $200. Several works by this artist, such as his Bird on Money, pay tribute to bebop musician Charlie Parker. A white taxi driver racially abuses a black man in a painting by Andy Warhol and this artist. In 2017, a work from this artist's Untitled series featuring a black (*) skull became the most expensive work sold at auction by an American artist. This neo-expressionist, who often used crowns in depictions of his heroes, collaborated with Al Diaz in a group that sprayed a four-letter motif in locations such as subway trains and public toilets. For 10 points, name this African-American artist from New York City, a member of the graffiti duo SAMO.

Bon Iver used this technique to produce the ghostly dissonance at the end of the instrumental track "Team." Billy Joel's "The Stranger" repeats the opening piano melody with a version of the melody played with this technique. Because Otis Redding died in a plane crash before he could sing the last verse, this technique is still the ending to "Sittin' on the Dock of the Bay." The J. Geils Band's "Centerfold" ends using this technique to (*) repeat the chorus theme. Instances of this sound follow every hook on a song whose rapper says, "I'm betting you like people / and I'm betting you love freak mode;" that song's hook says, "You just put your lips together / and you come real close." For 10 points, identify this musical activity that titles a suggestive Flo Rida hit.
2.c: 2015 STIMPY Pkt 10. Virginia A - Kentucky A Q5

2.q: This man presented Degas with the painting The Moon and the Earth after it received harsh criticism at the Durand Ruel exhibition. Among the Mangoes by this man depicts blacks on Martinique picking the title fruit during his stay on the island. Later, this artist painted (*) Spirit of the Dead Watching and another work that depicts a blue statue representing the "beyond" and Tahitian women in loincloths. For 10 points, name this French Post-Impressionist of works like Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going? And The Yellow Christ.

This person commissioned paintings on a study's walls of Tancred and Clorinda by Ambrose Dubois. Cupid and Juno bind two doves together over a split sphere in a painting commissioned for this person called The Council of the Gods. Veritas and a winged Saturn appear below this person and their son connected by the symbol of Concordia in the painting The Triumph of Truth. A man in black armor presented with a (*) portrait of this person by angels appears in a later painting watching as this person walks down a red-carpeted bridge in The Disembarkation at Marseilles. This woman and her husband appear as Juno and Jupiter at Lyon in a series of 24 paintings celebrating her rule and regency. For 10 points, name this French regent from an Italian noble family depicted in a cycle by Peter Paul Rubens.
2.r: Marie de' Medici [or Maria de' Medici; or Marie de Médicis; prompt on Marie or Maria or de Medici or de’ Medici]

2.q: The Aboriginal artist Lin Onus depicted a dingo in a parody of this work titled Michael and I are just slipping down to the pub for a minute. Camille Claudel used onyx and bronze for a sculpture similar to this work depicting three nude women holding hands. A photograph of Igor Stravinsky in Claude Debussy's apartment shows this work framed on the wall, which Debussy had earlier used as the cover for a set of "three symphonic sketches." This was the first work in a series that extensively used (*) Prussian blue imported from the Netherlands. This work, which was followed in its series by Fine Wind, Clear Morning, depicts three long fishing barges caught in the title phenomenon. The snow-capped Mount Fuji can be seen in the background of, for 10 points, what Katsushika Hokusai woodblock print depicting the title marine phenomenon?
2.r: The Great Wave off Kanagawa [or Under the Wave off Kanagawa]

2.q: Striking gold and blue scenes appear in "black" examples of these works. Literal interpretations such as a man touching his lips and holding a cup and the beatus vir planted "like a tree" appear in another of these works. An otter with a fish and overlapping snakes, lions, and peacocks adorn another of these works, which features a dense space-filling design named for (*) carpets. Lunettes in one of these works contain the zodiac signs against blue backgrounds. A procession of riders in May appears in that example of these works. Elaborate Chi-Rho monograms appear in Hiberno-Saxon-style examples of these works. The Limbourg brothers created a "Very Rich" example of these works for the Duke of Berry. For 10 points, miniatures fill the pages of what illuminated artworks?
2.r: books [accept illuminated manuscripts or psalters; accept Book of Hours; accept Book of Gospels; accept Utrecht Psalter; accept Book of Kells; accept Lindisfarne Gospels; accept Very Rich Hours of the Duke of Berry or Très Riches Heures du Duc de Berry] (The third clue refers to animals from the Chi-Rho monogram page in the Book of Kells.)

3.q: This painting was created during a trip the artist took after winning an honorable mention for his realistic painting of a weaver at his loom. A friend of this painting's artist claimed that it illustrated "in paradoxical, unforgettable form" the definition of a painting as a "flat surface covered with colours assembled in a certain order." This painting was created during a lesson by its artist's mentor, who told him "Is it quite green? Then put on green... that shadow, is it a bit blue? Don't be afraid to paint it as blue as possible." This painting, the most extreme example of the cloisonnist style, was painted on a (*) cigar box lid and nominally depicts the Bois d'Amour at Pont-Aven. The common name of this small painting derives from its influence on artists like Maurice Denis and Pierre Bonnard. For 10 points, name this abstract painting by Paul Serusier that kickstarted the Nabis group.
3.r: The Talisman [or Le Talisman; or The Aven River at the Bois d’Amour until “Bois” is read]

3.q: The only surviving work by an artist from this country depicts a view of a misty grove from a small boat. A contemporary artist from this country used hundreds of LED lights and plant debris to imitate works from this country for his piece Background Story. An artist from this country was asked by Picasso to criticize his work imitating this country's art and was later accused by James Cahill of creating a forgery entitled The Riverbank. In 2010, a work from this country was transformed into an animated version named after "wisdom." That work depicts a crowd of people yelling at a (*) boat about to crash into the Rainbow Bridge. That work depicts a scene during a title festival and was painted with an "ink-wash" style on a scroll. For 10 points, name this country shown in the work Along the River During the Qingming Festival by Zhang Zeduan.
3.r: China [or People’s Republic of China; or PRC; or Zhongguo] (the unnamed artists are Guan Daosheng, Xu Bing and Dong Yuan)

3.q: This artist took on caricaturist Marius de Zayas as an assistant and sent him to Europe as an art scout. A statement attached to one of his exhibitions proclaims "I was born in Hoboken. I am an American. The search for Truth my obsession." One of his earliest works showed children laughing near a woman gathering water and is entitled The Last Joke, Bellagio. Some of his abstract works only featuring clouds in the sky are called his Equivalents. This artist depicted a Dutch woman in the countryside in The Net Mender and horses being watered down in winter in The (*) Terminal. This man operated galleries called An American Place and The Intimate Gallery. His most famous work depicts the SS Kaiser Wilhelm II and people milling about its lower decks. For 10 points, name this artist of The Steerage, an American photographer who ran the gallery 291 and was married to Georgia O'Keefe.

In one painting by him, a dog urinates on the legs of a mustachioed blind man, who is selling matches. In one painting by him, a woman in an orange dress and cape, with a prominent sore on her lip, extends her naked right breast, and a man with a giant head has an anus for a mouth. In that work by him, on the back of a bent-over hag rides a child in pale yellow wearing a mask with a toothbrush mustache; those figures are in front of a figure in a skeleton suit wielding a scythe, with all three of these figures forming the shape of a (*) swastika. A saxophonist leans towards a dancing couple who stand to the right of a woman with giant pink ostrich feathers in the central panel of a work by him, whose left panel shows a WWI veteran with two wooden legs begging for money. For 10 points, name this leading artist of the New Objectivity movement, the painter of Seven Deadly Sins and the Metropolis triptych.

In this artist's depiction of a certain Biblical scene, scissors are seen in the foreground near a dog, as four soldiers take Samson away from Delilah. He depicts seven children standing in front of a statue of Mercury in his A Family Group. One of his works shows a woman in a blue dress standing next to Sir Jeffrey Hudson, a dwarf who has a monkey on his shoulder. This artist can be seen wearing a gold chain and medal while pointing to the title plant in Self-portrait with a Sunflower, which displays him wearing the honors he received from his patron, the husband of (*) Henrietta Maria. This artist depicted that patron dismounted, proudly standing "at the Hunt" in his distinctive Cavalier-style garb. For 10 points, name this Flemish artist, best known for serving as the court painter to Charles I.

In a study of this work, Steven White argued that the human genitalia on display are references to Aesop's fables. J. Bard McNulty identifies a woman from Northampton with a figure in this work who is invasively touched by a cleric. In this work, a house with five golden arches appears above a fallen horseman being pulled out of quicksand.Since 2016, the teacher Mia Hansson has been creating a replica of this work, which was likely designed by the (*) abbot Scolland. Bellringers appear below a dying monarch in this work who is depicted being carried to Westminster Abbey. Villagers look upwards at Halley's Comet in this work, whose most famous scene features an arrow entering a man's eye. For 10 points, Bishop Odo commissioned what work of embroidery, which chronicles the Norman invasion of England?
3.r: Bayeux Tapestry(“BYE-oh”) [or Tapisserie deBayeux; accept La telle du conquest or Tapete Baiocense]

3.q: A member of this family had the exterior of a building and the loggia across the street decorated with his trademark symbol of a sail blowing in the wind. 30 marble squares are inlaid in a funerary chapel named for this family in the San Pancrazio. An artwork that is [emphasize] actually named for this family is "carried in procession" in a painting by Frederic Leighton, but is incorrectly attributed in the painting's title.
